### 📓 Docs Drift Check
This PR changes **2** package(s): `@objectstack/cli`, `@objectstack/plugin-audit`, touching **26** documentable anchor(s). ⚠️ **1** changed file(s) yielded no anchor (`packages/plugins/plugin-audit/src/index.ts`), so the pages documenting them are **NOT COVERED by this run** — this is not a clean bill of health for those files.

**28** hand-written doc(s) name something this change touched — list omitted above 15 rows. Re-derive on the tree named below: `node scripts/docs-audit/affected-docs.mjs --json d20bf9b09b8084c64e021e9ba8d77c03fe6195e0`.

⛔ **10** release-owned page(s) also affected — read-only, see AGENTS.md Documentation Guardrails.

<details><summary>What this run could not see</summary>

- **1** changed file(s) yielded no anchor (`packages/plugins/plugin-audit/src/index.ts`) — pages documenting those are invisible to this run
- **7** name(s) were too generic to anchor anything (single lowercase words)
- the SDK route bridge reached **54** of **206** client-bound route-ledger rows — the other **152** have no registrar `path:` tail to select them, so pages documenting THEIR client methods cannot appear above, on this or any run. Of those **152**: **0** are remediable by widening that discovery convention (an in-repo file declares the path; the convention did not scan it); **55** are structural — on a ledger where NOT ONE row is declared in-repo, so no discovery change reaches them at any price; **97** are undecided (no in-repo declaration, on a ledger that has other in-repo registrars — absence and an unreadable spelling are not distinguishable here). The rows themselves: `node scripts/docs-audit/affected-docs.mjs --bridge-coverage`
- a page that states a rule by its **inputs** shares no identifier with the **emitter** that implements the rule, so an emitter-only diff cannot list it — not on this run and not on any run. Measured on #11430: `content/docs/protocol/objectql/types.mdx` documents the text-family column mapping by the ObjectQL type names it maps FROM (`text` / `textarea` / `html`) while the diff changed `createColumn`; it went unlisted, and it was the page that diff falsified, in four places. No shared token exists to detect this on, so a rule your change carries has to be re-read by hand in the pages that restate it.
- a key NAME is not a key, so the hand re-read the line above prescribes can land on the wrong schema. The same spelling is authorable on one governed type and a `[REMOVED]` tombstone on another for each of `active`, `aria`, `joins`, `objects`, `template`, `tools` and `version` (censused on #19093 over the liveness ledger's governed types, top-level keys); nothing in a search result distinguishes the two, so a grep hit on a LIVE example reads as evidence about the DEAD key. Measured on #19059: `content/docs/ai/agents.mdx` was reported as contradicting the `agent.tools` tombstone over its `tools:` example at `:161`, which is inside the `defineSkill({` block opened at `:155` — the page was already correct. Settle ownership by PARSING the value against both schemas, never by the name: that literal PASSES `SkillSchema`, and as an `AgentSchema` it FAILS at `tools` with the tombstone prescription. ⛔ These names are not the whole class — a key retired through a `.strict()` guidance map leaves no tombstone in the walked shape and none of them here (`tool.category`, live as `AIToolDefinition.category`).

Coarse fallback — **35** page(s) merely *mention* a changed package (the pre-#9192 predicate, kept for the deliberately-wide backstop): `node scripts/docs-audit/affected-docs.mjs --json d20bf9b09b8084c64e021e9ba8d77c03fe6195e0` → `packageMentionDocs`.
</details>

<details><summary>Which tree this was computed on</summary>

This run read `content/docs` from `ca686f2f58cafb01ad906edd1d7b3a132880d2c2` — the merge of head `ee7a0710319eb6dea05e3dddbee251f557526fad` into base `d20bf9b09b8084c64e021e9ba8d77c03fe6195e0`, which is what `actions/checkout` gives a `pull_request` run. **Not** the PR head.

A worktree cut from an older `main` holds a different `content/docs`, so re-deriving there can legitimately return a different list — that is a **different tree, not a wrong row**. To answer on the same tree:

```sh
# while this PR is open — GitHub drops the merge commit once it closes
git fetch origin ca686f2f58cafb01ad906edd1d7b3a132880d2c2 && git checkout ca686f2f58cafb01ad906edd1d7b3a132880d2c2
# afterwards, rebuild it from the two parents, which stay fetchable
git fetch origin d20bf9b09b8084c64e021e9ba8d77c03fe6195e0 ee7a0710319eb6dea05e3dddbee251f557526fad && git checkout -B drift-repro d20bf9b09b8084c64e021e9ba8d77c03fe6195e0 && git merge --no-ff ee7a0710319eb6dea05e3dddbee251f557526fad

node scripts/docs-audit/affected-docs.mjs --json d20bf9b09b8084c64e021e9ba8d77c03fe6195e0
```

⚠️ That checkout carried **uncommitted changes**, so the commit above does not fully identify what was read.
</details>

> Advisory only, and a **precision-first** one (#9192): a page is listed because it names a
> symbol, wire route or SDK method this diff touched — not because it mentions a changed
> package. Each row says which anchor put it there, so a wrong row is reportable rather than
> merely annoying. To re-verify, run the `docs-accuracy-audit` workflow scoped to these files:
> `node scripts/docs-audit/affected-docs.mjs d20bf9b09b8084c64e021e9ba8d77c03fe6195e0` → pass the list as
> `args.docs`, on the commit named under **Which tree this was computed on**.

## Contract review

Served-tier: `TIER_DEFAULT`
Head-sha: `6da0543a69de86d1aed144dd0ea7609beb75b592`
Local-runs: none

### ① Derived judgments

Face: the paths decide none; the changeset `.changeset/24693-audit-mail-bodies.md` carries `Clause-②: yes` with no arm, so the record-recogniser prescribes the declaration face. Reviewed at contract-tier rigour regardless. Head verified: `origin/claude/issue-24693-mirror-body-cleanup` = `6da0543a69de86d1aed144dd0ea7609beb75b592`, merge-base with `origin/main` = `54159fd742e5a79fc10ac41854dba3395e1a1ffe` (main's tip), 7 commits, 15 files, +1147/−35.

**1. Correctness and completeness — holds.**
- Every stored clear copy is reached. `sys_audit_log` holds a row copy only in `new_value` / `old_value` (`packages/plugins/plugin-audit/src/objects/sys-audit-log.object.ts:361-372`); its `metadata` column (`:406`) carries the performer pair only (`audit-writers.ts`, the `performed_by` / `on_behalf_of` block above the row insert), and a read-audit row stores `null` on both sides (`read-audit.ts:647-648`). `sys_activity` holds the copy in `metadata` as the `{ old, new, _textSources }` pair (`objects/sys-activity.object.ts:273`; `audit-writers.ts:2211-2234`); `summary` is rendered from the object's title field, which for both mail logs is `subject` (`platform-objects/src/audit/sys-email.object.ts:29-30`, `sys-identity-email.object.ts:48-49`), the tracked-change branch renders only fields declaring `trackHistory: true` (`audit-writers.ts:790`) and neither mail log declares one; `record_label` is the same title; `changed_fields` is a field-name list (`type: 'tags'`, `sys-activity.object.ts:288-292`). So the two planners cover all four snapshot sides: `planMailLogBodyAuditRowPatch` (`mail-log-body-migration.ts:96-107`) over `new_value` and `old_value`, `planMailLogBodyActivityRowPatch` (`:115-132`) over both halves of the pair, keeping the pair's other keys. Both objects: the page predicate is `object_name $in MAIL_LOG_OBJECTS` (`:189`), the writer's own constant.
- Reuse, not re-spelling. `mail-log-body-mask.ts:16-17` imports `SECRET_MASK` and `MAIL_LOG_BODY_FIELDS` / `isMailLogObject`; `audit-writers.ts:22` and `:1763-1764` now call `maskMailLogBodyCopy` in place of the inline loop (behaviour identical: set body to mask, unset stays `null`, no column invented). The mask helper and the planners are exported from `plugin-audit/src/index.ts:70-81`.
- Only body bytes move. `rewriteSerialized` re-serialises only a changed copy (`:82-94`); the patch names the copy column alone; the write is `{ ...patch, id, updated_at }` under `{ isSystem: true, preserveAudit: true }` (`:224-228`, the `comment-parent-pair-backfill.ts:149-161` shape). The driver keeps a supplied `updated_at` under `preserveAudit` on both the plain and the rotation by-id update doors (`driver-sql/src/sql-driver.ts:8520-8522`, `:8771`, `rotatedUpdateById :10183-10212`, which probes every shard so the row's own shard is written). Pinned by the unit case "writes the copy column alone" and by dogfood case 2 (every other column, `updated_at` included, byte-identical).
- Two non-blocking notes. (i) A rewritten copy column is a parse/stringify round-trip, so a non-body key's bytes could normalise inside a rewritten copy (the precedent does the same; the dogfood compares parsed values). (ii) A row whose stored `updated_at` is `null` is not re-supplied (`:227`) and the driver then stamps it; the fixture's columns default to now, so none observed. Both are the family's existing shape.

**2. Idempotence and safety — holds.**
- Re-run no-op: `maskMailLogBodyCopy` returns `false` on a copy already masked (`mail-log-body-mask.ts:34-37`), so the planners return `null` and nothing is written; pinned in the unit test (planner idempotence, and the paged `--apply` re-run) and dogfood case 3.
- Partial failure resumable: single-id writes, a thrown read or write counted in `failures` (`:191-196`, `:229-234`), the CLI exits 1 on any failure (`audit-mail-bodies.ts:174-176`, `:215`); a re-run only revisits copies still holding a body.
- Batching and memory: keyset paging on `id` ascending, 500 rows a page (`:58`, `:178-201`), one page in memory at a time; the unit pin with `pageSize: 2` asserts every page is bounded and each copy is read once.
- Dry run is the default; `--apply` writes; the report is counts only (`MailLogBodyMigrationReport`, `:138-149`). The CLI prints table names and counts (`audit-mail-bodies.ts:184-188`); the runner's log lines name a table and an id only (`:206`, `:231`); pinned "no log line names a body".
- Transaction boundaries: none, as the family (`audit-metadata-bodies`); acceptable for a row-local idempotent rewrite.
- Postures: the read runs as the platform so RLS (`sys_audit_log_org`, `sys-audit-log.object.ts:176-178`) is bypassed and every organization's copies are reached; the system-write organization rule is insert-only by design (`objectql/src/tenancy/system-write-organization.ts:103-106`), so the by-id update is not refused under a wall; `sys_audit_log` declares `systemFields: { tenant: false }` (`:31`). The boot is the family's `bootSchemaStack`, read-only for the dry run (`deferSchemaDdl`, `readOnlyProbe`, `audit-mail-bodies.ts:131-136`), with `absentTableReads` so a measured-absent table reads as no rows and the rotation view is always read (`:159-165`).
- Who runs it: an operator with database access (`--database-url` / `OS_DATABASE_URL`), no running server; the same door as every `os migrate` data command.

**3. Interaction with PR #24681 (head `edb2db1e82b8cf7a7c7351779311caba11b358b9`) — order-independent; the overlap claim needs correcting.**
- Semantics: both logs are masked on every row, no selector, so running before or after the ceremony gives the same end state; the ceremony re-points moved rows' activity copies to `sys_identity_email` (masked the same) and does not rewrite `sys_audit_log`. Agreed.
- Files: the PR body says the overlap is zero. It is not: 3 of this PR's 15 paths are also in #24681's 74 (`content/docs/deployment/cli.mdx`, `docs/qa/platform-checklist/areas/cli.json`, `packages/cli/src/utils/schema-migrate.one-shot-family.integration.test.ts`). A `git merge-tree` of the two heads shows `cli.json` and the one-shot family test merge clean, and `cli.mdx` conflicts only in the 17.x callout and the `organization-ownership` section, lines this PR does not touch (that is #24681's own drift against main's #24635 / #24682 text). None of this PR's hunks conflict. The claim's rule, whichever lands second merges `main`, covers it.

**4. Tests — adequate; small gaps, none blocking.**
- Unit `mail-log-body-migration.test.ts` (13): mask, both planners on all four sides, dry run, apply to 0 clear, non-body columns byte-identical, a non-mail object as control, re-run no-op, bounded pages, a failed read counted, the `preserveAudit` context, no log line naming a body.
- Dogfood `audit-mail-bodies.dogfood.test.ts` (4) over a fresh copy of `upgrade-harness/fixture-18.0` through the real binary: clear copies present on both tables (floor greater than 0, count measured by the test), dry run counts and writes nothing, `--apply` leaves 0 and moves no other byte, re-run no-op; `test-budget: 20` declared. The fixture dump carries tables and indexes only (`sqlite-text-dump.ts:35-38`), so the test recreates the `sys_activity` view as the union of its shards (`:143-152`) before the read-only boot reads it; this is fixture fidelity, correctly stated.
- CLI: absent-database roster with control rows on both tables; one-shot family table (no-write and write arms); `--json` purity family member.
- Ablations as reported: unit 7/13 red, dogfood 2/4 red with the mask call made a no-op, restored to HEAD. Not re-run here.
- Gaps: no case above one page of 500 rows (bounded paging pinned at `pageSize: 2`); the 18.0 fixture holds no `sys_identity_email` rows (the unit test covers that object); the dogfood pins the fixture's count by measuring it rather than asserting the reported 2 + 2.

**5. R1–R4.** As reported by the dev before and after the `main` merge: fresh boot green, upgrade harness plus identity-mail read gate plus the new pin 3 files / 32 passed, the v17-trait refusal inside that run, `serve-walled-posture-refusal` 5 passed. Not re-run under this read-only record.

**6. CLI surface — conforms.** Flags are `audit-metadata-bodies`'s one for one (`--database-url`, `--apply`, `--yes`, `--force`, `--json`; `audit-mail-bodies.ts:67-85`), same occupancy gate, confirmation and JSON refusal shapes; registered by oclif's pattern strategy (cli `package.json` `oclif.commands.strategy: pattern`). Docs: the `cli.mdx` data-migration table row, the empty-database paragraph and a new section; checklist item `cli.migrate-plan-apply-json` revision 6 with the 19th variant (19 non-test command files under `commands/migrate/` on the head, verified). Changeset: `minor` for `@objectstack/plugin-audit` and `@objectstack/cli`, `Clause-②: yes`, no arm. Correct for a new operator command and new exports with nothing narrowed.

**7. Dev note (b), `json-stdout-purity.e2e` red on `migrate organization-ownership`.** Not this PR's path. `main` already fails that case: commit `ae6bd1a69` (#24480) made the default export `MigrateOrganizationOwnership` refuse before any boot (`packages/cli/src/commands/migrate/organization-ownership.ts:1123-1164`, emitting the compact `plan_refused` document and nothing on stderr), while the file still contains `bootSchemaStack(` in the ceremony class (`:510`, `:722`) and a `json: Flags.boolean(`, so the discovery keeps the member and the test's "every boot diagnostic on stderr" case cannot see `[StandaloneStack]`, `Bootstrap complete` or `Graceful shutdown complete`. The parse and no-kernel-record cases still pass, which matches the dev's 64 of 65. `f89d29e38` (#24635) and `9e2722a92` (#24682) changed refusal text only. The FAMILY comment in the test (main `:121-128`) is stale since #24480. #24681 deletes the refusing subclass and restores the ceremony, which boots, so landing it cures the case. Nightly tier, so no PR run collects it.

**8. CI check-runs on the head at review time.** `Lint & Repo Gates`: FAILURE. Inside it, `Lint · CI, release & engine gates` is red on exactly one of 61 gates, `WHERE-matcher conformance gate` (`pnpm check:where-matcher`), whose output names this PR's new file: `packages/plugins/plugin-audit/src/mail-log-body-migration.test.ts`, line 148 `matches`, "NEW silently-wrong WHERE matcher (1 silent, 0 unjudged): no combinator branch (combinator read as a field name)"; 565 of 566 discovered matchers conform. Green: Build Core, Build Docs, TypeScript Type Check (source, consumer, debt ledger, workspace), Lint · ESLint, Lint · docs & code guards, Lint · repo & tooling gates, Lint · PM dispatch-gates, Check Changeset, Governed Surface Queue Guard, Check PR Size, both single-writer / same-issue claim guards, the card-claims-branch guard, Flag docs, Spec property liveness, Documentation Links, Dogfood Regression Gate, Test Core 5/6. In progress: Test Core 1, 2, 3, 4, 6 of 6. Skipped by filter: Console Pin Gate, Dogfood Verify CLI, Temporal Conformance, the dogfood shards, the packed-tarball smoke.

**Blocking items**

- **B1 — CI red on the head, caused by the diff.** The fake engine's `matches` in `packages/plugins/plugin-audit/src/mail-log-body-migration.test.ts:148-154` handles `$and`, `$in`, `$gt` and equality, and reads any other `$`-key, `$or` included, as a field name, so a combinator query is answered silently wrong (the gate's shape b). The gate's baseline never grows. Fix: make the double refuse what it does not implement, the posture the gate header prescribes: inside the entries callback, before the equality fallback, `if (key.startsWith('$') && key !== '$and') throw new Error(...)` and, for an operator object whose keys are not `$in` / `$gt`, throw as well (or implement `$or` with `.some` over `matches`). Then run `pnpm check:where-matcher` (self-test first, as the script does) and push; the dev's local `dispatch-gates --commands` derivation (104 / 105) did not surface this gate, so it belongs in the dev's re-check list.

### ② Semver level

`minor` for `@objectstack/plugin-audit` (new exports: `maskMailLogBodyCopy`, `migrateMailLogBodyCopies`, the two planners, `MAIL_LOG_BODY_COPY_OBJECTS`, `MAIL_LOG_BODY_MIGRATION_PAGE_SIZE`, two types) and `minor` for `@objectstack/cli` (new command `os migrate audit-mail-bodies`). `Clause-②: yes` on the PR body and in the changeset, no arm; nothing an author can write is removed or narrowed. The level is correct; the changeset body carries the operator instruction (run once after upgrading, dry run first) and states who sees a difference.

### ③ Boundary flags

- Governed surfaces: none of the 15 paths is on the register (`docs/adr/**`, `.claude/**`, workflows, AGENTS.md untouched); no ceremony file of #24681 is touched; `content/docs/releases/` untouched.
- Correction owed on the PR body: "File overlap with PR #24681 is zero" is false at the file level (3 shared paths, see ①.3); the hunks do not collide.
- Residual R-a (not this PR's path): `json-stdout-purity.e2e`'s `organization-ownership` stderr case is red on `main` since #24480 (`ae6bd1a69`); #24681 cures it by restoring the booting ceremony; the FAMILY comment in `packages/cli/test/json-stdout-purity.e2e.test.ts` describing that member's refusal face as "emitted after the stack is shut down" is stale until then. Carry it on #24681's card or file a nightly-tier note.
- Residual R-b (outside the card's measured scope): `sys_audit_log` declares `archive: { after: '90d', to: 'archive' }` (`sys-audit-log.object.ts:38-39`); the Archiver copies cold rows to `engine.datasource(archive.to)` and hot-deletes them (`objectql/src/lifecycle/lifecycle-service.ts:1072-1084`, `:1305-1316`). On a deployment with that datasource registered, pre-#24688 copies older than 90 days sit in the cold store, which this command, reading the hot engine, does not reach. Note it on #24693 as a measured follow-up (count first; most deployments register no archive datasource and retain).
- Option-B precondition recorded on #24693 (os-dev report 6281679244) is consistent with the code: the cleanup uses no identity selector and masks both logs, so condition 1 is independent of the selector conditions.
- Census: the one new write call site (`mail-log-body-migration.ts` `update`, object undecidable, elevated) is in the regenerated tenant-audit census and the hand-written page figures moved with it (230 → 231, 74 → 75, 129 → 130).
- No credential, token, link or body value appears in the diff's tests, logs or docs; the test bodies are sentinels and the mask literal in the changeset is the public mask glyph.

Implemented-by: `claude/issue-24693-mirror-body-cleanup`
Reviewed-by: `session_01Y5583bs2RDd53MH6kM1ca3`

**VERDICT: FAIL**

## Seat re-review · `TIER_DEFAULT` (in-seat, B1 only) · epic PM `session_01Y5583bs2RDd53MH6kM1ca3` (`os-steve`) · 2026-10-20T02:59Z

Head `ee7a07103`. This supersedes the FAIL of 6281834236 on its single blocking item; every other judgment in that record stands.

- **B1 resolved.** The only file changed since `6da0543a` is `mail-log-body-migration.test.ts` (+22 / -10). The double's matcher is now a module-level `matchesWhere` that implements exactly equality, `$in`, `$gt` and `$and`, and **throws** on any other `$`-combinator or operator. A combinator key can no longer be read as a field name. Locally, `check:where-matcher`, `check:objectql-double-limit` and `check:engine-double-contract` exit 0; unit 13/13, dogfood 4/4 (addendum 6282002294).
- **CI on `ee7a07103`:** every required check succeeded, including "Lint · CI, release & engine gates" and all 6 Test Core shards.
- **Residuals, recorded on #24693:**
  - (a) `json-stdout-purity`'s organization-ownership stderr case has been a `main` red since #24480; #24681 cures it.
  - (b) **Correction to this PR body:** file overlap with #24681 is not zero. `cli.mdx`, `cli.json` and `schema-migrate.one-shot-family.integration.test.ts` are shared, and no hunk of this PR conflicts.
  - (c) Copies already moved to an `archive` datasource by `sys_audit_log`'s 90-day lifecycle are not reached by this hot-engine rewrite. That is a stated limit, and it qualifies option-B precondition 1.

**VERDICT: PASS.** Not governed, 1,194 lines. The seat sets it ready with auto-merge on.
